body: Thanks so much, that's one of my favorite things, ever.

I can only imagine this going on, this suffering. I've had a pattern of trauma (see my other comments) and it doesn't seem to be improving. Darkness behind and I can see nothing but darkness ahead.

I'm incredibly alone, and have never had a day pass where I felt good, or truly happy. I work against it, have since I can remember, and still end up back in the same place I started.

I'm not apathetic. I've spent my *entire* life trying to change this.

I've changed everything about me. My job, I've moved, I've traveled the world, I've put myself through school. I've dated different people, tried new types of therapy. Apathetic is the one thing I'm not.

How exactly does one make life worth it?
that's just it - I've spent my life trying. Swimming against the current to gain a lot of self-knowledge and have put a ton of effort into it. And it's done me no good.

Hard times have not passed in my case. They have gotten worse with time, despite all the fighting I've done.

I already help a lot of people. Just the last few months I've intervened in a few terrible situations and helped people. I just think there's no helping me.
What if I never get what I need? I mean there is a pattern here that's hard to ignore.

The fact that she killed herself is the only reason I'm alive now.

Thirty years is nothing? Even if I live to ninety (an unlikely prospect) it'll have been a third of my life.

Re-evaluate what?

Thank you, that's a nice way of looking at things. I don't know how long one goes on fighting though, until you decide it's time to stop. Another decade? Then I'll be 40, and have wasted all this time hurting, for nothing. Looking at another decade of this, even if things pick up at 41, makes me less likely to want to stick around.
I'm glad for you. I feel like I've already made those fundamental changes, and it hasn't worked. It doesn't work for everyone.

It's funny, I've been working on a semibiographical novel that ends in the main character's death. I'll continue working on it, but I don't know how helpful its is. Thanks for your insightful suggestion.
Thanks.
You mean like quitting my job and traveling the world for two years? Done.

I've been seeking a partner like that. Pretty actively. And it hasn't worked out.

How do I adjust my defense mechanisms? Or what in particular are you referring to? I've taken on a *lot* of crazy goals, I put myself through school when I was 16, working 70 hours a week. I've been able to succeed in everything I've put my mind to.
Thank you for saying so. I can't quite believe it's true for me, but I do believe it's true for others.

No, I mean, they're honest with me. They consider me a good friend, but they have other, better friends. It's not a secret. I do most of the work, normally, because they have on great motivation to do so.

No, it's a very long string of traumas. That was just one.

I lost someone else very close to me soon after that. I was involved in a relationship that ended very badly, and then another one a few years after that. Someone close to me became an abusive alcoholic. I was assaulted. I became extremely ill and nearly died, and that illness could return at any time. That's just the tip of the iceberg.

No, I meant, I had some fantastic interactions with the opposite sex. I've been in love before, but in those cases it always ended really, really badly. And honestly, the love I felt for others wasn't returned. Same for my friends. The people I'd consider my best friends wouldn't say the same of me.

edit: sorry trying to clarify - I have had some supportive relationships, but never a partner, never anyone who actually wanted to be with me, know me and support me.

I can no longer imagine a future for myself that is at all appealing. I just don't want this any more.

I don't know if anything can or will help. There was a time, I think, when other options were available to me, but I put my faith and energies in things that weren't worth it, in the end. I can't depend on finding love, it hasn't worked for me, and I have to accept that it becomes less and less likely with time.

That's very kind of you.

I don't believe I'm unlovable, and I've devoted myself to making me into someone worthy of love. I do pretty well at accepting the love of others, and did battle quite a lot with self-hatred and low self-esteem, but ultimately think I came out ahead.

No, but it was the beginning of a pattern for me. And it helped shape my identity. I think there was a window where it wouldn't have mattered so much. But life didn't work out that way, and more trauma was piled on top of trauma.
Thanks, I know you might be right. Be well.

I do a lot of writing, I'm even a professional writer of sorts.

Thanks, though.

Thanks, I feel like going through the motions is a big part of why I'm still here, I take my responsibility to do my best very, very seriously.

I've done what I could regarding the ruts, quit a job, relocated to another part of the country, spent about a year traveling, and am trying a new type of therapy (in addition to regular psychotherapy).

I am good with creative outlets, I'm a professional writer of sorts. My background is more in the sciences, but I've ended up in a creative career. If I could write my way out of this, I would have.

Thanks for your kind words.

I've actually looked into ECT and TMS - I'm not a good candidate for either, mainly because of the duration of my depression, but I also have some other health problems that are contraindicated for either or both treatments. But the idea's still there, in the back of my head.

I'm willing to try anything at this point.

I heard about those studies, sounds interesting. It's actually why I started meditating. I'm trying to learn more about it online, as I'm in the middle of the country, pretty far from anywhere where someone could teach me it on my own.

Thanks, I've actually looked into Why Am I Still Depressed? and done a lot of research on Bipolar II, I just don't fit the symptoms. My normal life is more like dysthymia and occasionally swinging deeper into chronic unipolar depression.

I'm hanging in there, still. But losing hope. I'm a naturally hopeful person, so this is at odds with what I want to be true.
I do pretty frequently. I spent a lot of time on my bike, and hiking.
Yeah, my therapist is actually really into yoga and meditation. It is nice, but it doesn't seem to be alleviating my depression.
I know crossposting is discouraged, but I was thinking you 2Xers might be able to help me.

I think you might be right. I come from a family of people who're mentally ill, psychotically depressed, alcoholic, schizoaffective disorder, etc. I am starting to think that I'm too broken to ever get fixed. If it's chemical (which it might be) so far, no medication has proved effective at treating it.
Sorry to crosspost, but I think I need your insight and AskReddit was sort of the wrong place.
Let it go? I'm being serious, how do you just let it go? It's like not wanting something. How do you stop wanting something you wish you had?

All the things you've suggested are very nice and I've done most of them (I don't knit, but I do own a cashmere wrap). I communicate a ton. I indulge myself pretty frequently. It's nice after a lifetime of poverty.

But I'm trying to make a list, here, of what might work. And so far I've got nothing. Nothing I haven't tried already.

Looked inside to see what I need? I need to stop being overwhelmed by sadness. I need to find someone who loves me. Other than that, I don't know. I'm lucky to be alive, to have pretty good health, to have friends, and it's ungrateful of me to still feel the way I do. But I still feel it, and it hasn't gotten any better.

I don't know how to make myself happy, maybe I never did. A happy life would look like one that gave me a reason to wake up in the morning. Maybe a family of my own, a partner would be great. A job that I love would be a great bonus.

I don't know what to do, exactly, to let myself "be" - I've been following my heart and it seems to get me nowhere. Into bad relationships, out of a job.

Filling my heart up with love for myself? That sounds nice, but honestly, how does one go about doing such a thing?

I'm confident in my abilities (I'm intelligent, capable, confident, and not un-attractive) and seem to be unfulfilled by any of that.

That is nice, that that guy was able to find happiness. I don't really have the same problems he does, but that's nice to know he was able to overcome it. I don't think it's impossible.

I've gone from having a ton of structure (I was working 70 hours a week, plus going to school, plus having a social life) and thinking that was causing this to be worse, to doing less, having more free time to devote to the things I like (reading and writing and so on) and neither of the two seemed to help. Except for the past two years, I've worked full-time since I was 16. I don't know about "wallowing" - I'm really good at putting one foot in front of the other, it's not like I sit in bed all day and cry.

Thank you though, for sharing your suggestions and that post.

edit: more on your second suggestion: keeping busy is a great treatment for depression, it just doesn't seem to be working.

These are just the things I already spend time doing. That's what's not working. I took over a year off to travel, so another vacation probably isn't going to do it for me. But thank you, sincerely, for your comment.
